overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by discussing an unlisted citizen statement at its June 27 meeting. A 2014 allegation was dismissed as untimely, and the late complaint response was noted as a reminder only.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the Board violated the Open Meeting Law in the past, citing a 2014 example.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that this allegation is untimely and we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board should not have accepted and discussed an unlisted written citizen statement about the complainant at the June 27 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: A public body may discuss an unnoticed topic that arises for the first time during a meeting, provided that the chair did not reasonably anticipate such topic at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; AG noted the Board responded to the complaint after the 14-business-day deadline and issued a reminder.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the complaint was filed with the Board on July 25, and the Board did not respond until August 29.

allegations.summary: Complainant contended the citizen's written statement contained inaccurate statements about him, which the AG said would not be an Open Meeting Law violation even if true.
allegations.key_passage: Even if this allegation is true, it would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint implied the complainant should have received individualized notice before being discussed at the open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: a public body is not required to provide individualized notice before discussing an individual in open session.
